newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl sees good chances for coal compromise talks.
newsitem.headline: Kohl sees good chances for coal compromise talks.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Wednesday he saw good chances of reaching an agreement over planned cuts in coal subsidies when he meets German mining union leader Hans Berger on Thursday.
Kohl told journalists in Munich he favoured a step-by-step approach that would help ease the effect of the deep cuts he wants to make in subsidies for the industry by the year 2005.
Speaking after meeting business leaders at a trade fair, Kohl said he was optimistic the two sides could reach an agreement "with a bit of good will."
Miners in Germany's 18 pits walked out on Friday after Bonn said it would cut subsidies to 3.8 billion marks ($2.2 billion) by 2005 instead of to a promised 6.5 billion marks.
Bonn argues it can no longer afford to pay over nine billion marks a year to compensate users for a domestic coal price which is over three times the world market price.

Thousands of coal miners have paralysed Bonn's government district for three days running but began leaving on Wednesday so Kohl, who called off a meeting with Berger on Tuesday, would come back to the table on Thursday.
